summary: Techno: 125–140 BPM, relentless kick, 16th hats, almost no harmony: one stab or drone, change by automation
body: Drums: kick on every beat, closed hats in 16ths, open hat off-beats, clap or rim on 2 and 4; percussion loops of odd lengths.
Harmony: one minor chord or a single stab repeated, sometimes i–VII; melody is rare. Detroit techno has more chords, Berlin/minimal less.
Movement comes from slow automation: filter cutoff, delay feedback, reverb sends; parts enter every 16 or 32 bars.
Bass: a rumble (the kick through a dark reverb) or a short off-beat sub.

Apply: pattern/four-on-the-floor on the drums, then pattern/prog-techno-characteristic-1 on the keys four bars later. It leaves tempo and sounds to you: move the tempo toward 125–140 gradually, and swap sounds from the links.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one
